title: Rs 1,142 Crore Released To Panchayats In MP, Jharkhand, Punjab And Mizoram Under Fifteenth Finance Commission Grants
text:
Infrastructure
Swarajya Staff
Mar 26, 2026 | Updated 10:06 AM GMT+5:30

The Union Government has released over Rs 1,142 crore to rural local bodies in Madhya Pradesh, Jharkhand, Punjab and Mizoram during the financial year 2025–26 as part of the Fifteenth Finance Commission's untied grants.
The funds will empower grassroots governance and enable need-based local development in Panchayati Raj Institutions across these states.
Madhya Pradesh received the largest allocation of Rs 631.91 crore as the second instalment for 51 eligible district panchayats, 300 block panchayats and 22,933 gram panchayats.
An additional Rs 1.26 crore from the withheld portion of the first instalment was also released to four block panchayats and 19 gram panchayats.
Jharkhand secured Rs 269.03 crore as the first instalment for 23 district panchayats, 264 block panchayats and 4,344 gram panchayats, with an additional Rs 3.65 crore released from previously withheld funds.
Punjab received Rs 222 crore for 13,262 gram panchayats, 150 block panchayats and 22 district panchayats, while Mizoram was allocated Rs 14.80 crore for all 816 eligible village councils.
The grants are recommended by the Ministry of Panchayati Raj and the Ministry of Jal Shakti before being released by the Ministry of Finance in two instalments annually.
The untied grants can be utilised by panchayati raj institutions to meet location-specific needs under the 29 subjects listed in the Eleventh Schedule of the Constitution, excluding salaries and establishment costs.
The Fifteenth Finance Commission had allocated a total of Rs 2.4 lakh crore for rural local bodies across India for the period 2021-26.
These funds are distributed amongst states based on population and area, with 90 per cent and 10 per cent weightage respectively, ensuring equitable development across rural India.
